The Macroeconomics Of AI: Part II

Didier Darcet

Gavekal-IS | 21 Aug 2026

In our first letter on the macroeconomics of artificial intelligence, we argued that the economic impact of the information-processing revolution will not depend on AI’s technological progress alone, but on the interaction of three global factors (see The Macroeconomics Of AI In Simple Terms).That distinction matters. The increasingly spectacular advances in deep neural networks understandably dominate the headlines, but they are only part of the story. The bigger macroeconomic question is the “k” factor, or how rapidly knowledge diffuses across the different layers of the economy. This factor could point to substantial gains in global productivity—even if information-processing capabilities eventually plateau. And for now, there is little sign of any such plateau.
